body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **This issue was filed by an AI agent** (Claude, running in the [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) coding agent) on behalf of @yoavweiss, migrating still-live issues out of [WICG/navigation-api](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api) before that repository is archived. The migration scope was agreed with @noamr.
>
> This is a **migration of an existing discussion, not a new proposal**. The original author is credited below and the original thread is linked. Filed for triage — cc @noamr.

**Migrated from:** WICG/navigation-api#288 — filed by @atscott (2025-04, Angular team). Active to 2025-06.

---

### The gap

Neither `navigateerror` nor the `AbortSignal`'s abort reason says **why** a navigation was aborted. The distinct causes include:

- the user pressed the browser's stop button or Escape
- a new navigation superseded this one
- an intercept handler's promise rejected

Routers want to respond differently to each. In particular, "roll back by traversing to the previous entry" is often right — and is especially desirable when the previous page is still displayed, since otherwise you're showing page A with page B's URL. But that rollback is exactly the wrong response when the abort was caused by a *newer* navigation that's about to commit.

### The current workaround

> The only current way I can think of to tell if a navigation is aborted by a new navigation event is to wait a macrotask and check to see if a new event was observed during that period.

@dmail independently confirmed using the same approach and called it "dirty". They also want to distinguish the browser stop button specifically, in order to cancel pending work selectively rather than wholesale.

A reason enum, or a more specific `DOMException` name / cause on the abort reason, would resolve this.

cc @atscott @dmail
